In modern times, this name has been chosen for babies in Muslim communities around the world, reflecting the importance placed on moral character and honor in Islamic society.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Raghaad represents one's innate potential for goodness, nobleness, and righteousness. It serves as a reminder of the divine nature of the human spirit and the importance of cultivating virtuous qualities in one's life. Embracing this name can inspire the bearer to strive for personal growth and moral improvement, ultimately bringing them closer to their Creator.

historical_references.reference: Ibn Abd al-Hakam, Al-Futuh, p. 163-164. 10th century CE. Raghaad was a city in the Jazira region, which is present-day northern Iraq and southeastern Turkey.
historical_references.context: Raghaad is mentioned as the site of a major battle between the Muslim forces under Caliph al-Mu'tasim and the Byzantine forces under Emperor Romanos I Lekapenos. The battle, fought in 883 CE, ended with a decisive Muslim victory, allowing al-Mu'tasim to secure his control over the region.

historical_references.reference: Ibn al-Jawzi, Tarikh al-Islam, vol. 11, p. 103. 12th century CE. Raghaad was a significant religious center in the Abbasid Caliphate.
historical_references.context: Raghaad is mentioned as the site of a famous Sufi gathering led by the mystic Sheikh Abu Abd Allah al-Bakkar al-Jurjani. The gathering, which took place in 1125 CE, attracted thousands of Sufi scholars and seekers from all over the Islamic world.

The modern context of Raghaad reflects the global reach and accessibility of Islamic culture and its representation in digital spaces.
